learningStrategy.title: Keep .NET as your backend advantage; add AI engineering depth
learningStrategy.summary: You already have nearly four years of enterprise backend experience. This roadmap does not restart you as a beginner: it applies your C#, ASP.NET Core, SQL, security, and architecture skills to modern AI systems. The main portfolio projects use ASP.NET Core 10. Python remains a secondary skill you can add later if a target role specifically requires it.

steps.title: Learn AI concepts through .NET
steps.detail: Refresh modern async/streaming patterns only as needed, then learn model behavior and .NET AI abstractions.

steps.title: Build secure AI APIs
steps.detail: Use ASP.NET Core 10, Microsoft.Extensions.AI, your enterprise backend strengths, and production API practices.

steps.title: Build RAG and evaluation
steps.detail: Create document ingestion, embeddings, pgvector retrieval, citations, and repeatable evaluation.

steps.title: Add controlled agents and production safeguards
steps.detail: Integrate business tools with permissions, approvals, security, cost controls, deployment, and observability.

steps.title: Ship proof and prepare for remote .NET AI roles
steps.detail: Complete a capstone, polish portfolio evidence, and practice AI backend/system design interviews.

learningStrategy.rule: Use the linked docs, implement the practical exercise, then complete the tasks. Move on when the readiness check is true—not just when the week ends.

weeks.title: Modern C# for AI Services
weeks.objective: Refresh only the C# features that make AI backend code asynchronous, typed, testable, and safe.
topics: Records, nullable reference types, generics, and result models
Task, ValueTask, CancellationToken, and async streams
Dependency injection, options, typed HttpClient, and configuration
Unit tests, mocks, and structured logging

tasks.text: Create a .NET 10 Web API solution with nullable reference types and analyzers enabled.
Build a typed service using records, options, DI, and cancellation-aware async methods.
Use IAsyncEnumerable<T> to stream sample events and test client cancellation.
Add unit tests and structured logs for success, validation failure, and cancellation.

weeks.deliverable: A clean .NET 10 service foundation with async tests and streaming.

steps: Records, nullable reference types, generics, and result models
Task, ValueTask, CancellationToken, and async streams
Dependency injection, options, typed HttpClient, and configuration
Unit tests, mocks, and structured logging
learningGuide.practice: Use your existing C# experience; focus on async stream cancellation and current .NET APIs, not beginner syntax.
learningGuide.readyWhen: You can explain cancellation propagation and stream typed events without blocking the request thread.

weeks.title: LLM and Generative AI Foundations
weeks.objective: Understand the model concepts needed to design reliable applications without trying to train a foundation model.
topics: Tokens, context windows, sampling, model inference, and latency
Hosted versus local models, quantization, privacy, and cost
Embeddings and similarity at a conceptual level
Model limitations, nondeterminism, and hallucination

tasks.text: Compare responses from one hosted model and Ollama using the same test prompts.
Measure response latency and token usage for short and long contexts.
Write a concise model-selection note for a privacy-sensitive enterprise workflow.
Create a C# console experiment that records model, prompt version, duration, and outcome.

weeks.deliverable: A model comparison report backed by a repeatable C# experiment.

steps: Tokens, context windows, sampling, model inference, and latency
Hosted versus local models, quantization, privacy, and cost
Embeddings and similarity at a conceptual level
Model limitations, nondeterminism, and hallucination
learningGuide.practice: Learn model behavior and tradeoffs before choosing frameworks; use the same scenarios to compare providers.
learningGuide.readyWhen: You can describe context limits, nondeterminism, privacy, latency, and cost tradeoffs for two providers.

weeks.title: The .NET AI Stack and Provider Abstractions
weeks.objective: Use .NET AI abstractions to keep application code testable and portable across providers.
topics: IChatClient and IEmbeddingGenerator abstractions
Provider adapters for hosted and local models
Microsoft.Extensions.AI middleware, logging, and OpenTelemetry
Test doubles and deterministic application tests

tasks.text: Register a provider behind IChatClient with configuration from options.
Write one application service that works with two provider adapters.
Add a fake chat client and unit tests that do not call a live model.
Instrument model calls with duration, provider, and error telemetry.

weeks.deliverable: A provider-switchable .NET AI service with deterministic tests.

steps: IChatClient and IEmbeddingGenerator abstractions
Provider adapters for hosted and local models
Microsoft.Extensions.AI middleware, logging, and OpenTelemetry
Test doubles and deterministic application tests
learningGuide.practice: Treat the model as a dependency behind an interface, just as you would a database or payment gateway.
learningGuide.readyWhen: The same application tests pass with a fake provider, Ollama, and a hosted provider.

weeks.title: ASP.NET Core 10 AI API Fundamentals
weeks.objective: Build typed HTTP contracts for AI features using ASP.NET Core 10 Web API.
topics: Controllers and Minimal APIs, endpoint groups, and OpenAPI
Request/response validation and ProblemDetails
DI scopes, configuration, options validation, and HttpClientFactory
Rate limits, cancellation, health checks, and API versioning

tasks.text: Create an AI API with chat, health, and model-capability endpoints.
Add validated request records and consistent ProblemDetails responses.
Configure provider settings with validated options and secret-safe logging.
Document APIs with OpenAPI and test contracts using WebApplicationFactory.

weeks.deliverable: A documented ASP.NET Core 10 AI API shell with reliable validation.

steps: Controllers and Minimal APIs, endpoint groups, and OpenAPI
Request/response validation and ProblemDetails
DI scopes, configuration, options validation, and HttpClientFactory
Rate limits, cancellation, health checks, and API versioning
learningGuide.practice: Keep endpoint handlers thin: validate the request, call an application service, return a typed result.
learningGuide.readyWhen: OpenAPI describes the contract, invalid requests return useful 4xx errors, and cancellation reaches the model call.

weeks.title: Production .NET API Architecture and Testing
weeks.objective: Apply your backend experience to AI endpoints while keeping boundaries and tests clear.
topics: Application and infrastructure boundaries
EF Core or Dapper for relational access
Transactions, idempotency, and database migrations
Integration tests, Testcontainers, and API contract tests

tasks.text: Define domain, application, and infrastructure boundaries for an AI workflow.
Persist conversations and request metadata with EF Core or Dapper.
Add integration tests for data access and API behavior.
Document transaction, retry, idempotency, and failure boundaries.

weeks.deliverable: A tested .NET API vertical slice with persistent conversation metadata.

steps: Application and infrastructure boundaries
EF Core or Dapper for relational access
Transactions, idempotency, and database migrations
Integration tests, Testcontainers, and API contract tests
learningGuide.practice: Use familiar clean architecture patterns only where they clarify AI workflow responsibilities; avoid layering for its own sake.
learningGuide.readyWhen: A new developer can trace a request from endpoint through application service to persistence and tests.

weeks.title: Identity, Authorization, and Tenant Isolation
weeks.objective: Secure AI features using identity and authorization rules already familiar from enterprise systems.
topics: JWT/OIDC authentication and claims
Role and resource-based authorization
Tenant-aware data access and prompt/context isolation
Secrets, input limits, upload safety, and audit trails

tasks.text: Secure AI endpoints with the chosen identity provider and explicit policies.
Enforce tenant filters in both conversation and document retrieval paths.
Add audit events for model requests and sensitive tool actions.
Test unauthenticated, unauthorized, cross-tenant, and oversized-input cases.

weeks.deliverable: An authenticated .NET AI API with tested tenant isolation.

steps: JWT/OIDC authentication and claims
Role and resource-based authorization
Tenant-aware data access and prompt/context isolation
Secrets, input limits, upload safety, and audit trails
learningGuide.practice: Model authorization before writing AI prompts; the model must never decide whether the caller is permitted.
learningGuide.readyWhen: Automated tests prove one tenant cannot retrieve another tenant’s records or documents.

weeks.title: Streaming, Background Work, and Resilience
weeks.objective: Handle slow model calls and long-running AI tasks without fragile request behavior.
topics: Server-Sent Events with ASP.NET Core 10
BackgroundService, queues, and durable job options
Timeouts, bounded retries, circuit breakers, and backpressure
Redis caching and coordination where appropriate

tasks.text: Stream tokens or progress using the ASP.NET Core 10 SSE result APIs.
Move document ingestion to a background worker with job status persistence.
Add timeouts and bounded retries for transient provider failures.
Use Redis for one explicitly scoped cache or coordination use case and test invalidation.

weeks.deliverable: An AI API with streaming responses and reliable background ingestion.

steps: Server-Sent Events with ASP.NET Core 10
BackgroundService, queues, and durable job options
Timeouts, bounded retries, circuit breakers, and backpressure
Redis caching and coordination where appropriate
learningGuide.practice: Keep long-running ingestion out of the request lifecycle and make user-facing streaming cancellable.
learningGuide.readyWhen: A cancelled client stops unnecessary work, and failed jobs can be inspected and retried safely.

weeks.title: RAG Architecture and Retrieval Quality
weeks.objective: Design retrieval around evidence quality, access boundaries, and explainable results.
topics: Ingestion, extraction, metadata, and stable document identities
Chunking by structure, size, and overlap
Dense, lexical, and hybrid retrieval
Filters, reranking, relevance thresholds, and citations

tasks.text: Draw a RAG data flow and define document/chunk metadata.
Compare chunking strategies on a small representative enterprise corpus.
Implement lexical and vector retrieval with tenant and permission filters.
Return ranked evidence with source IDs, page references, and relevance scores.

weeks.deliverable: A retrieval benchmark showing relevant chunks and source traceability.

steps: Ingestion, extraction, metadata, and stable document identities
Chunking by structure, size, and overlap
Dense, lexical, and hybrid retrieval
Filters, reranking, relevance thresholds, and citations
learningGuide.practice: Inspect what retrieval returns before tuning generation; poor evidence cannot be fixed by a stronger prompt.
learningGuide.readyWhen: For representative questions, you can explain why each source was retrieved and why inaccessible sources are excluded.

weeks.title: Embeddings and Vector Search in .NET
weeks.objective: Generate embeddings through .NET abstractions and store/query vectors with PostgreSQL and pgvector.
topics: Embedding dimensions and similarity metrics
IEmbeddingGenerator and provider-specific adapters
Vector schema/indexes and distance operators
Batching, metadata filters, and embedding model versioning

tasks.text: Add an embedding provider using IEmbeddingGenerator.
Create a pgvector schema with document, tenant, chunk, and model-version metadata.
Implement vector search and combine it with a lexical query.
Measure retrieval quality and latency across representative queries.

weeks.deliverable: A .NET embedding and hybrid-search service using PostgreSQL/pgvector.

steps: Embedding dimensions and similarity metrics
IEmbeddingGenerator and provider-specific adapters
Vector schema/indexes and distance operators
Batching, metadata filters, and embedding model versioning
learningGuide.practice: Version embeddings with their model and ingestion configuration so re-indexing is deliberate.
learningGuide.readyWhen: You can explain the chosen metric, index, metadata filters, and how embeddings are regenerated after model changes.

weeks.title: Document Ingestion and Secure Knowledge Stores
weeks.objective: Build a production-minded ingestion pipeline before adding answer generation.
topics: PDF/text extraction and file validation
Chunk provenance, page references, and deduplication
Background ingestion, retries, and deletion workflows
Document-level and tenant-level authorization

tasks.text: Create an upload endpoint with size/type checks and tenant ownership.
Extract text and create chunks with page and document metadata.
Queue embedding and index work with retry-safe status transitions.
Implement document deletion that removes source text and vectors.

weeks.deliverable: A secure document ingestion pipeline with traceable chunk provenance.

steps: PDF/text extraction and file validation
Chunk provenance, page references, and deduplication
Background ingestion, retries, and deletion workflows
Document-level and tenant-level authorization
learningGuide.practice: Treat uploaded documents as untrusted input and make deletion semantics explicit across original files and derived data.
learningGuide.readyWhen: Every chunk can be traced to an authorized source document and deletion removes its searchable content.

weeks.title: Grounded RAG Answers and Citations
weeks.objective: Connect retrieval evidence to useful responses while making unsupported answers explicit.
topics: Prompt construction and bounded context
Citation identifiers and evidence-to-answer mapping
Abstention when evidence is weak or missing
Streaming with source metadata and partial failures

tasks.text: Build a RAG application service that receives authorized evidence only.
Generate answers with citation markers tied to retrieved chunk IDs.
Return an explicit insufficient-evidence response when thresholds are not met.
Stream answer events and citations using an API contract tested by clients.

weeks.deliverable: A cited document-answer endpoint with a tested abstention path.

steps: Prompt construction and bounded context
Citation identifiers and evidence-to-answer mapping
Abstention when evidence is weak or missing
Streaming with source metadata and partial failures
learningGuide.practice: Keep citations grounded in retrieved evidence and verify citation IDs server-side.
learningGuide.readyWhen: Tests verify all citations point to retrieved authorized chunks and weak retrieval does not produce confident unsupported claims.

weeks.title: RAG Evaluation and Regression Testing
weeks.objective: Measure retrieval and answer quality so RAG changes can be reviewed rather than guessed.
topics: Golden datasets and expected evidence
Retrieval recall/ranking and answer faithfulness
Model-as-judge limits and human review
Regression thresholds, prompt versioning, and experiment records

tasks.text: Create a versioned evaluation dataset from realistic questions and source passages.
Measure retrieval recall and citation correctness separately from answer quality.
Compare two chunking or reranking configurations.
Run evaluation from CI on a small deterministic subset and save reports.

weeks.deliverable: An evaluated ASP.NET Core Enterprise Knowledge Assistant with ingestion, pgvector retrieval, grounded citations, and a documented quality baseline.

steps: Golden datasets and expected evidence
Retrieval recall/ranking and answer faithfulness
Model-as-judge limits and human review
Regression thresholds, prompt versioning, and experiment records
learningGuide.practice: Evaluate retrieval and generation separately; one aggregate score can hide failure causes.
learningGuide.readyWhen: You can explain retrieval failures from an evaluation set and demonstrate citation correctness, tenant isolation, and safe abstention in the working assistant.

weeks.title: Tool Calling and Bounded AI Workflows
weeks.objective: Let models request business tools while keeping execution under normal application controls.
topics: Tool/function schemas and structured outputs
Tool allowlists, input validation, and result shaping
Execution budgets and explicit stop conditions
Separating model planning from application authorization

tasks.text: Expose a read-only customer lookup tool with validated parameters.
Use structured output for tool arguments and reject malformed requests.
Limit tool count, execution time, and response size.
Record a trace of model request, selected tool, validated arguments, and result.

weeks.deliverable: A bounded assistant that performs one safe, read-only business lookup.

steps: Tool/function schemas and structured outputs
Tool allowlists, input validation, and result shaping
Execution budgets and explicit stop conditions
Separating model planning from application authorization
learningGuide.practice: The model can suggest a tool call; only your application can authorize and execute it.
learningGuide.readyWhen: Tool arguments are validated, access is checked against the caller, and every run has an enforced budget.

weeks.title: Semantic Kernel and Agent Workflows
weeks.objective: Orchestrate multi-step .NET AI workflows with explicit state and controlled tools.
topics: Semantic Kernel plugins and function choice
Agent/workflow state and bounded execution
Microsoft Agent Framework concepts and orchestration
Human approval and persistence boundaries

tasks.text: Build a Semantic Kernel plugin around a narrow business capability.
Model a workflow with explicit states, transitions, and a human approval point.
Persist resumable state without storing secrets or untrusted instructions as policy.
Compare a deterministic workflow with an agent loop and justify the tradeoff.

weeks.deliverable: A resumable .NET AI workflow with a human approval checkpoint.

steps: Semantic Kernel plugins and function choice
Agent/workflow state and bounded execution
Microsoft Agent Framework concepts and orchestration
Human approval and persistence boundaries
learningGuide.practice: Prefer deterministic workflows when business steps are known; add agent choice only where it creates measurable value.
learningGuide.readyWhen: You can diagram state transitions and show the exact approval boundary before a side effect.

weeks.title: Enterprise System Integration and Governance
weeks.objective: Connect AI workflows to ERP/CRM services while preserving identity, tenant, and audit boundaries.
topics: API adapters and anti-corruption boundaries
Claims/tenant propagation and permission checks
Approval workflows and audit logging
Idempotent writes and policy enforcement

tasks.text: Integrate a mock ERP customer/invoice API through a typed adapter.
Apply role and tenant checks inside each tool execution.
Require human approval for write operations and persist approval identity.
Create audit records linking user, model run, tool, approval, and outcome.

weeks.deliverable: An AI Business Assistant that reads authorized records and gates writes for approval.

steps: API adapters and anti-corruption boundaries
Claims/tenant propagation and permission checks
Approval workflows and audit logging
Idempotent writes and policy enforcement
learningGuide.practice: Keep business authorization in application services, not in prompt text or model-generated plans.
learningGuide.readyWhen: Cross-tenant and unauthorized actions are blocked in tests; approved actions are auditable and idempotent.

weeks.title: Reliable Agents and Failure Handling
weeks.objective: Make AI workflows predictable under model, tool, and infrastructure failures.
topics: Transient/permanent failure classes
Retries, deadlines, cancellation, and idempotency
Agent loops, tool call budgets, and safe stops
Prompt injection defense and observability

tasks.text: Inject provider timeout, malformed tool arguments, and downstream API errors.
Retry only safe operations and apply idempotency keys to writes.
Set max steps, token budget, wall-clock deadline, and cancellation paths.
Add adversarial prompt-injection cases and record safe rejection behavior.

weeks.deliverable: A Secure ERP Action Assistant built with ASP.NET Core: bounded tool workflows, role and tenant checks, approval-gated writes, audit history, and adversarial tests.

steps: Transient/permanent failure classes
Retries, deadlines, cancellation, and idempotency
Agent loops, tool call budgets, and safe stops
Prompt injection defense and observability
learningGuide.practice: Never retry a non-idempotent side effect blindly; retries need operation identity and explicit safety rules.
learningGuide.readyWhen: Every action is permission-checked by application code, consequential writes require explicit approval, and timeout/retry/injection cases have repeatable tests.

weeks.title: AI Application Security and Prompt Injection
weeks.objective: Threat-model the full AI request path and implement defense in depth.
topics: Direct/indirect prompt injection and untrusted retrieved content
Data exfiltration, tenant leakage, and tool abuse
Output validation, content handling, and secret protection
Security testing and incident-ready audit trails

tasks.text: Write a threat model for chat, RAG, streaming, and tool execution.
Add retrieval permission checks and output validation at service boundaries.
Test malicious documents, tool argument injection, and sensitive-data requests.
Review logs and traces to ensure prompts/secrets are not accidentally exposed.

weeks.deliverable: A security test suite and threat model for an AI backend.

steps: Direct/indirect prompt injection and untrusted retrieved content
Data exfiltration, tenant leakage, and tool abuse
Output validation, content handling, and secret protection
Security testing and incident-ready audit trails
learningGuide.practice: Prompt injection is a risk to contain, not a string pattern that can be perfectly filtered.
learningGuide.readyWhen: Every high-risk threat has a control, owner boundary, and automated test or documented residual risk.

weeks.title: Performance, Cost, and Model Routing
weeks.objective: Tune AI systems based on measured quality, latency, and cost.
topics: Token accounting and prompt/context efficiency
Provider/model selection and fallback policies
Semantic caching and tenant-safe cache keys
Concurrency, batching, rate limits, and load behavior

tasks.text: Capture baseline latency, token use, and answer quality per representative workflow.
Add a model routing policy for quality/cost or local/hosted constraints.
Implement tenant-safe caching with explicit invalidation.
Load-test streaming and retrieval endpoints; compare measured tradeoffs.

weeks.deliverable: A performance report with a quality-preserving cost or latency improvement.

steps: Token accounting and prompt/context efficiency
Provider/model selection and fallback policies
Semantic caching and tenant-safe cache keys
Concurrency, batching, rate limits, and load behavior
learningGuide.practice: Optimize only after collecting baseline measurements and protect quality with the evaluation set.
learningGuide.readyWhen: Your report documents baseline, intervention, result, and quality/security checks.

weeks.title: Deployment and .NET 10 Operations
weeks.objective: Package and deploy the AI API with repeatable configuration and safe operations.
topics: Docker and Docker Compose
Secrets and environment-specific configuration
CI/CD tests, migrations, and image publishing
Reverse proxies, TLS, health/readiness, and cloud deployment

tasks.text: Containerize the ASP.NET Core API and its worker.
Run PostgreSQL/pgvector and Redis through Compose for local development.
Build CI steps for tests, migration checks, and container creation.
Deploy a demo and document configuration, backup, rollback, and health checks.

weeks.deliverable: A deployed .NET AI service with a repeatable local and CI workflow.

steps: Docker and Docker Compose
Secrets and environment-specific configuration
CI/CD tests, migrations, and image publishing
Reverse proxies, TLS, health/readiness, and cloud deployment
learningGuide.practice: Keep secrets out of images and source; deployments should be reproducible from repository instructions.
learningGuide.readyWhen: A clean checkout can run locally and the deployed service exposes useful health/readiness signals.

weeks.title: Observability and Production Reliability
weeks.objective: Operate AI applications with useful traces, metrics, and privacy-aware diagnostics.
topics: Structured logs, metrics, traces, and correlation IDs
AI model and embedding telemetry
Worker and queue observability
SLIs, alerts, health endpoints, and incident debugging

tasks.text: Instrument API, retrieval, embedding, model, and tool boundaries.
Track latency, errors, token/cost usage, and queue age without logging secrets.
Define an SLI for response latency and ingestion completion.
Simulate a provider incident and write a short operational runbook.

weeks.deliverable: An observable AI service with a runbook for provider and worker failures.

steps: Structured logs, metrics, traces, and correlation IDs
AI model and embedding telemetry
Worker and queue observability
SLIs, alerts, health endpoints, and incident debugging
learningGuide.practice: Use telemetry to locate a failing stage while minimizing sensitive data collection.
learningGuide.readyWhen: A trace explains one end-to-end request and an operator can follow the runbook to diagnose a simulated outage.

weeks.title: Enterprise .NET AI Architecture
weeks.objective: Design a maintainable, multi-tenant AI backend that fits enterprise systems.
topics: Bounded contexts, service boundaries, and API versioning
Tenant-aware persistence and authorization
Queues, consistency, and failure isolation
Capacity planning and provider abstraction

tasks.text: Create an architecture diagram for the capstone and mark trust boundaries.
Record decisions for storage, provider selection, background processing, and tenancy.
Define API contracts and database constraints for conversations/documents/tools.
Review failure modes, scaling assumptions, and migration strategy.

weeks.deliverable: A reviewable architecture pack with decisions and failure analysis.

steps: Bounded contexts, service boundaries, and API versioning
Tenant-aware persistence and authorization
Queues, consistency, and failure isolation
Capacity planning and provider abstraction
learningGuide.practice: Reuse existing enterprise strengths, but make model, retrieval, and tool boundaries explicit.
learningGuide.readyWhen: A reviewer can challenge your tradeoffs and see how security, scale, and failure handling are addressed.

weeks.title: Enterprise AI Assistant Platform
weeks.objective: Combine the skills into a secure, provider-flexible .NET AI application.
topics: Provider abstraction and model configuration
RAG, citations, and conversation history
Permissioned tools, workflow state, and streaming
Evaluation, observability, and security controls

tasks.text: Implement provider selection through Microsoft.Extensions.AI abstractions.
Integrate tenant-safe RAG with citation and abstention behavior.
Add a controlled business tool with role checks and human approval.
Connect streaming, evaluation, OpenTelemetry, and admin configuration.

weeks.deliverable: A portfolio-grade multi-tenant Enterprise AI Assistant Platform built with ASP.NET Core 10, RAG, controlled tools, evaluation, and production observability.

steps: Provider abstraction and model configuration
RAG, citations, and conversation history
Permissioned tools, workflow state, and streaming
Evaluation, observability, and security controls
learningGuide.practice: Integrate only the AI capabilities you can evaluate, secure, and operate.
learningGuide.readyWhen: A demo shows provider swap, cited RAG, an authorized tool, approval, streaming, and telemetry.

weeks.title: Portfolio Quality and Public Demonstrations
weeks.objective: Turn implementation work into credible evidence a remote employer can review.
topics: Repository structure, architecture documentation, and API examples
Automated tests, deployment scripts, and security notes
Demo recording and clear project narrative
Accurate CV and GitHub presentation

tasks.text: Polish the .NET Task API and AI Document Intelligence repositories.
Write READMEs with architecture, setup, API examples, tests, limitations, and threat controls.
Publish diagrams and short demos showing tradeoffs rather than only UI output.
Make one project easy to launch with Docker Compose and seeded non-sensitive data.

weeks.deliverable: Two polished .NET portfolio repositories and concise demo materials.

steps: Repository structure, architecture documentation, and API examples
Automated tests, deployment scripts, and security notes
Demo recording and clear project narrative
Accurate CV and GitHub presentation
learningGuide.practice: Make the evidence reproducible and be precise about what is learning work versus professional experience.
learningGuide.readyWhen: A reviewer can launch the project, run tests, understand architecture, and see a working AI flow.

weeks.title: Remote .NET AI Career Preparation
weeks.objective: Prepare for AI backend interviews while positioning your enterprise .NET background accurately.
topics: C#/.NET and ASP.NET Core interview fundamentals
LLM, RAG, evaluation, agent safety, and AI system design
Behavioral stories from enterprise backend experience
Remote communication, CV, LinkedIn, and application tracking

tasks.text: Practice explaining the AI Document Intelligence architecture and evaluation choices.
Complete practical exercises in async .NET APIs, SQL, security, and RAG.
Prepare examples of tradeoffs, failures, and measurable project outcomes.
Apply to .NET AI Engineer, AI Backend Engineer, and enterprise AI application roles.

weeks.deliverable: A truthful CV, interview portfolio, and focused remote .NET AI application plan.

steps: C#/.NET and ASP.NET Core interview fundamentals
LLM, RAG, evaluation, agent safety, and AI system design
Behavioral stories from enterprise backend experience
Remote communication, CV, LinkedIn, and application tracking
learningGuide.practice: Target job descriptions that value your .NET enterprise history and AI application skills.
learningGuide.readyWhen: You can explain a production-minded AI system, defend its tradeoffs, and accurately describe your Python as secondary learning.
